title: Isometric-bundle path heat bound retains holonomy and yields discrete Nash

statement.quantifiers: M>=1,k>=1 integers; X=CP2, fiber CP1 with probability measures, actual reversible unitary plane transports; EVERY integer 1<=t<=min(M+1,k^2); every g in L2 with finite vertical energy.
statement.assertion: H_M uses K_M=d_M|<v,w>|^(2M), d_M=(M+1)(M+2)/2; B_t=H_M^t exp[-t C_V/k^2]. ||B_t||_(1->infinity)<=430 d_M k^2/t^3. ||g||_2^2<=t(E_H+E_V/k^2)+h_B(t)||g||_1^2. General path kernel bound h_X(t)h_V(s) requires compatible fiber isometries, not flatness.
assumptions: Transport inverses/isometries and invariant vertical heat; reversibility for Nash.
C_V spherical eigenvalues ell(ell+1); H_M strongly commutes with vertical heat.
Discrete integer powers; H_M HS spectrum may be negative.

inputs: Explicit base kernel, geometric transports and analytic fiber heat.
outputs: Connection-retaining scalar smoothing/Nash bound with actual finite time window.
interface.precision: Exact Berezin beta_ell=M!(M+2)!/[(M-ell)!(M+ell+2)!], zero for ell>M.
costs: Integrated geometric variables are proof coordinates, not free frame/side information.
Analytic scalar theorem does not implement sampler, channel, encoder or circuit.
Rank consequence needs separate actual source score/symbol contracts.

proof_mechanism: Expand positive kernel over horizontal paths; transport remains inside vertical heat argument, bounded by uniform fiber supremum.
Finite CP2 spectrum gives h_X<=86 d_M/t^2, CP1 heat h_V<=5/s.
Joint spectral inequality 1-b^t exp(-tc/k^2)<=t(1-b)+tc/k^2 for b in [-1,1].
obstructions: beta_0=1 prevents extending pure t^-2 estimate beyond acquired window.
Integrated coherent-symbol contraction does not hold pointwise.
Cannot multiply cold and hot memory bounds without SAME-symbol contracts.

potential_uses.transfer_gate: Acquire destination reversible base heat and transport-invariant fiber smoothing rather than substituting a product geometry.

review.source_reported: Internal analytic audits or released-source proof only; exact reported scopes retained in cited source. No scientific suite or formal kernel replay in this extraction.
